candidates.title: The Help Desk Husband
candidates.one_line_concept: He enters the kitchen to help, then asks so many tiny questions that she becomes the kitchen GPS.
candidates.emotional_truth: Sometimes love shows up with good intentions, but the mental load still follows her.
candidates.humor_angle: Every helpful act begins with, 'Where is...?'
candidates.relatable_trigger: The husband who wants to help but cannot find the salt in his own house.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: This is us. He is sweet, but please learn one drawer.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Easy partner-tag for couples where one person is the kitchen command center.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People will list the funniest things their partner cannot find.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: He said, 'I'll help.' Then asked 17 questions.
suggested_slide_arc: He opens every cabinet except the right one.
She is cooking and answering like a helpline.
Final beat: he washes dishes without asking; she softens.

candidates.title: One Pyaaz, Seven Bartans
candidates.one_line_concept: He chops one onion with full MasterChef confidence and somehow uses half the kitchen.
candidates.emotional_truth: Domestic love is laughing at the mess without dismissing the effort.
candidates.humor_angle: The scale of destruction is wildly larger than the task.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Partners who help with one step but leave a full cleanup episode behind.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Guilty. Also why is this exactly my husband?
candidates.why_people_may_share: It is specific enough to feel personal and broad enough for couple tags, family groups, and married friends.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People will compare the one-task messes their partners create.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: He chopped one pyaaz. The kitchen needed recovery time.
suggested_slide_arc: She asks him to chop one onion.
He gets serious: board, knife, three bowls, towel, extra plate.
He presents the chopped onion like a trophy.
She smiles at him, then points to the sink.

candidates.title: His Signature Dish: Moral Support
candidates.one_line_concept: He helps by tasting, giving commentary, adjusting the flame, and standing very lovingly in the way.
candidates.emotional_truth: Sometimes companionship is inefficient, but still quietly comforting.
candidates.humor_angle: He contributes opinions, appetite, and one suspiciously timed hug.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The partner who turns cooking into a two-person activity without doing the main work.
candidates.likely_audience_reaction: Annoying but cute. Unfortunately, I love this version.
candidates.why_people_may_share: Feels more intimate than complaint-based content, so it is saveable and sendable.
candidates.why_people_may_comment: People will debate whether moral support counts as kitchen help.
candidates.suggested_text_hook: He came to help. Became live commentary.
suggested_slide_arc: He walks in with confidence and a spoon.
He tastes, suggests salt, blocks the drawer.
She gives him one look; he grins.
Final beat: he feeds her the first bite and quietly cleans the counter.

top_pick.reason: It has the strongest 3-second hook, cleanest visual proof, broadest couple relatability, and a built-in comment prompt without making the husband look cruel or useless.

engagement_rationale: SS_02 should drive shares because it is hyper-specific, visual, and instantly taggable: one small kitchen task becoming a full cleanup story.
distribution_risks: Avoid making the wife look like a scolding parent.
Keep the mess premium and warm.
Keep the joke on the situation, not male incompetence.
